DECISIVE PER-STAGE BREAKDOWN (the brief's fallback ask -- can a batched dense n=1024 solver clear the per-call floor?):
- cuSOLVER whole batch = 107ms (benchmark). nsys: cuds_symv 28% (768 inst) + gemvx 19% (2338) + gemv2T 8.5% (1070) + sytrd4 8.2% = ~64% memory-bound serial tridiag; laed D&C ~8ms; back-transform ~few ms.
- Batched tridiag SOLVE (Triton Sturm-bisect + twisted): 4.6ms bisect + 2.4ms twisted + 17.9ms orthonormalize = ~25ms warm. FAST, competitive. Back-transform GEMM: negligible.
- THE WALL is the REDUCTION. Fine per-op breakdown of the PyTorch blocked-Householder (instrumented): corr 172ms + wform 101ms + symv 92ms + q1v(eigenvector accum) 82ms + norm 30ms = ~430-580ms. The trailing rank-2b GEMM the brief wanted on tensor cores is ONLY 5ms -- ALREADY efficient. The wall is the ~1023 SEQUENTIAL per-column PyTorch ops, each memory-bound + ~5-6x a fused kernel's cost. Variants all lose: pyhh blocked 540ms, unblocked (no corrections) 429ms, fp16-panel-symv 576ms (net-neutral -- the aggregate of small serial ops, not the symv alone, is the cost). All ~4-5x cuSOLVER's WHOLE runtime.
- The ONLY fused-kernel reduction available (the C-CTA cluster kernel; k=1024 -> C=5 forced by the 111000-halves SMEM cap, so 60x5=300 CTAs -- NOT grid-starved like the b=8 sign-DC use) runs at 156ms warm / 227ms benchmark. Barrier-bound: the cross-cluster cl.sync per column serializes each matrix's 5 CTAs (the brief noted this resists tuning; PB sweep is anti-correlated). RAW cluster G is orth_max/gate~109 on ~12/60 ill-cond mixed matrices; a prescaled (power-iter top-sigma) FP32 NS(4) rescues 10, leaving 2/60 with a MISSING/duplicate eigenvector (eigr_rel 19x gate) that NS cannot recover -> cuSOLVER (cheap). Best custom result: cluster + NS(4) = shape 7 188913us = 1.77x cuSOLVER (t4).
- Shape-7 structure (60 matrices): 8 PR<85 (steep/low-rank), 30 PR[85,120) (dense -- the brief's ~28 genuinely-dense), 9 PR~166, 3 PR~222 (nearrank), 10 PR>=400 (5x571.9, 5x1024==flat/identity-like). hom_ratio 18.7, twolevel_frac 0.083. Very heterogeneous.

CONCLUSION (measured, not reasoned): a batched dense n=1024 solver in PyTorch/Triton CANNOT clear the 107ms floor -- the reduction is a hard sequential-per-column wall. The fused cluster kernel gets closest (1.77x) but is barrier-bound.
